document_metadata.title: 1、INT. BANK VAULT - DAY
document_metadata.summary: A sealed manuscript from Dr. Watson reveals unpublished cases of Sherlock Holmes, including a 1887 Yorkshire murder, withheld for their sensitive and scandalous nature.

entities.name: Iron gate opens and bank guards enter vault
entities.description: An iron gate opens, allowing two bank guards to enter a secure vault area within a bank in London.

entities.name: Guard switches on lights in the vault
entities.description: One of the bank guards activates the lighting system inside the vault, illuminating the shelves lined with strong-boxes, document cases, and wrapped packages.

entities.name: Guards locate Watson's tin dispatch box
entities.description: The two bank guards search along the shelves and find a battered tin dispatch box labeled JOHN H. WATSON, M.D.

entities.name: Guards remove dispatch box and place it on table
entities.description: The guards take the tin dispatch box from the shelf and set it down on a table for examination.

entities.name: One guard dusts off the dispatch box
entities.description: While the other guard prepares to open it, one of the bank guards cleans dust from the surface of the dispatch box.

entities.name: Guard cuts sealed cord with scissors
entities.description: Using a pair of scissors, one of the guards cuts through the heavy cord securing the dispatch box, breaking the wax seals on the knots.

entities.name: Guard unlocks and opens the dispatch box
entities.description: The guard inserts the key strung on the cord into the lock of the dispatch box, turns it, and lifts the lid to reveal its dusty contents.

entities.name: Guards begin removing items from the dispatch box
entities.description: The guards start taking out various objects from the opened dispatch box one by one, including personal effects and mementos.

entities.name: Opening Of Watson'S Sealed Dispatch Box
entities.description: A procedurally conducted retrieval and opening of a long-sealed tin dispatch box belonging to Dr. John H. Watson in a London bank vault, revealing artifacts from his association with Sherlock Holmes.

relations.subject: John H. Watson
relations.relation_name: refers to as Holmes's mysterious brother
relations.description: Watson mentions Mycroft Holmes in a neutral but respectful manner within the manuscript, characterizing him as 'Holmes's mysterious brother.' This reflects a momentary expression of acknowledgment or reference, not an established ongoing relationship. The mention occurs within a single narrative moment (reading the text), so the persistence is momentary.

relations.subject: John H. Watson
relations.relation_name: refers to as the devilish Professor Moriarty
relations.description: Watson refers to Professor Moriarty in the manuscript with negative characterization ('devilish'), indicating a momentary expression of disdain or antagonism within the narrative context. This reflects a situational attitude rather than an established ongoing hostile relationship, so 'unfavorable_toward' is appropriate.

relations.subject: Sherlock Holmes
relations.description: Holmes solved the baffling murder of Colonel Abernetty, which reflects a specific, action-based interaction in the past. Since this is a one-time investigative act and not evidence of an ongoing relationship, it best fits 'favorable_toward' as a momentary cooperative or protective action, rather than a stable or phase-level relationship. The text does not support 'interacts_with' as it is not an allowed type, and no other allowed relation clearly captures a solved crime. 'favorable_toward' is chosen as the closest valid proxy for a beneficial action toward the victim posthumously, grounded in the explicit statement of solving the murder.

document_metadata.title: 12、INT. DRESSING ROOM - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Rogozhin spreads a false rumor about Watson and Holmes, causing the dancers to shun Watson, who realizes the misunderstanding too late and confronts Rogozhin.

entities.name: Rogozhin introduces Sherlock Holmes to Madame Petrova
entities.description: Rogozhin announces the arrival of Sherlock Holmes to Madame Petrova, presenting him with the phrase 'Ja priviol vam Mistera Sherlock Holmesa, dorogaia'.

entities.name: Madame Petrova greets Sherlock Holmes
entities.description: Madame Petrova extends her hand to Holmes and says 'Otchen rada', formally welcoming him to her dressing room.

entities.name: Sherlock Holmes kisses Madame Petrova's hand
entities.description: In response to her greeting, Holmes takes Madame Petrova's hand and kisses it as a gesture of courtesy.

entities.name: Madame Petrova comments on Sherlock Holmes's height
entities.description: After appraising Holmes, Madame Petrova remarks in Russian that he is shorter than she expected, which Holmes then translates aloud.

entities.name: Rogozhin dismisses the importance of physical stature
entities.description: Rogozhin responds to the comment about Holmes's height by stating that such things do not matter—what counts is intelligence.

entities.name: Madame Petrova expresses admiration for Sherlock Holmes's adventures
entities.description: From her dressing table, Madame Petrova declares that she has read all of Holmes's adventures and particularly praises the story of the Hound of the Baskervilles.

entities.name: Madame Petrova begins undressing behind the paravent
entities.description: Madame Petrova rises, moves behind a screen, and starts undressing while continuing to speak with Holmes, her head remaining visible.

entities.name: Rogozhin presents a violin to Sherlock Holmes
entities.description: At Madame Petrova's request, Rogozhin retrieves a violin from its case and hands it to Holmes for inspection.

entities.name: Sherlock Holmes examines the violin
entities.description: Holmes inspects the violin closely, reads the label inside, checks its shape and varnish, and plucks the strings to assess its tone.

entities.name: Sherlock Holmes identifies the violin as a genuine Stradivarius
entities.description: After examination, Holmes concludes that the violin is an authentic Stradivarius from the master's best period.

entities.name: Madame Petrova offers the Stradivarius to Sherlock Holmes as a gift
entities.description: From behind the paravent, Madame Petrova instructs Rogozhin to give the Stradivarius to Holmes as a present in anticipation of services he will provide.

entities.name: Rogozhin confirms the gift of the Stradivarius to Sherlock Holmes
entities.description: Rogozhin tells Holmes that the violin is his, explaining that it is a gift from Madame Petrova for services yet to be rendered.

entities.name: Sherlock Holmes expresses disbelief at receiving the Stradivarius
entities.description: Holmes is astonished by the offer, noting that while his fees are high, a Stradivarius is an extraordinary and unexpected gift.

document_metadata.title: 31、INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Gabrielle Valladon, attacked and nearly killed, seeks Holmes' help to find her husband Emile, who vanished after joining a fake company; Holmes plans to trace replies to a blank letter sent to Emile's last known address.

entities.name: Gabrielle arrives in London searching for her husband
entities.description: Gabrielle travels to London in pursuit of her missing husband, Emile, a mining engineer, after his letters abruptly stop and she discovers his employer does not exist.

entities.name: Holmes deduces Emile's occupation from Gabrielle's wedding ring
entities.description: Holmes observes that Gabrielle's wedding ring is made of copper and infers that her husband worked in a copper mine in the Congo, which she confirms.

entities.name: Gabrielle reveals Emile's invention and employment by Jonah Limited
entities.description: Gabrielle explains that her husband invented a new air pump and was hired by an English company called Jonah Limited, prompting her to join him in London.

entities.name: Gabrielle discovers the Jonah Limited address is an empty store
entities.description: Gabrielle visits the listed address of Jonah Limited on Ashdown Street and finds it to be an abandoned storefront with no sign of the company.

entities.name: Gabrielle learns that Jonah Limited does not exist
entities.description: After investigating, Gabrielle confirms that Jonah Limited is not a registered or operating company, raising suspicions about her husband's disappearance.

entities.name: Police dismiss Gabrielle's missing persons report with little urgency
entities.description: Gabrielle files a missing persons report with the police, but they respond without enthusiasm or immediate action.

entities.name: Belgian embassy refers Gabrielle to Holmes
entities.description: The Belgian embassy, after hearing Gabrielle's account of her missing husband, recommends that she seek the assistance of Sherlock Holmes.

entities.name: Watson offers Gabrielle a cup of coffee during the consultation
entities.description: During the meeting at Holmes's residence, Watson courteously hands Gabrielle a cup of coffee as she recounts her story.

entities.name: Holmes examines the return address on Gabrielle's letters
entities.description: Holmes inspects the envelope from Gabrielle's correspondence and reads the return address, identifying it as Ashdown Street.

entities.name: Gabrielle expresses unwavering trust in her husband's honesty
entities.description: When questioned by Holmes about the possibility of deception, Gabrielle firmly asserts that her husband would never lie to her, citing their deep mutual love.

entities.name: London
entities.description: The city where Gabrielle arrives to search for her husband and where she consults Holmes.
entities.summary: London is a major city in England where current events unfold, serving as the destination for Holmes and Gabrielle's search for her missing husband, following arrangements made in Venice.

entities.name: Congo
entities.description: The country where Gabrielle and Emile were married and where Emile previously worked in a copper mine.
entities.summary: The country where Gabrielle and Emile were married and where Emile previously worked in a copper mine.

entities.name: Ashdown Street
entities.description: The street address associated with Jonah Limited, where Gabrielle found only an empty store.
entities.summary: The street address associated with Jonah Limited, where Gabrielle found only an empty store.

entities.name: three weeks ago
entities.description: A relative time reference indicating when Gabrielle's husband's letters stopped arriving.

entities.name: Gabrielle
entities.description: A woman who has traveled to London in search of her missing husband, Emile Valladon, a mining engineer she married in the Congo.
entities.summary: A woman is found injured and disoriented near Westminster Bridge, brought to Holmes and Watson with amnesia, later seen in Watson's room and reuniting emotionally with Holmes before disappearing, leaving her clothes behind.

entities.name: Emile Valladon
entities.description: Gabrielle's husband, a mining engineer who worked in a copper mine in the Congo and invented a new kind of air pump, leading to his employment by Jonah Limited.
entities.summary: Gabrielle Valladon's husband, a mining engineer and inventor of a new air pump, worked in a Congo copper mine and was employed by Jonah Limited; his corpse was found in a coffin and identified by Gabrielle, Holmes, and Watson.

entities.name: Sherlock Holmes
entities.description: A consulting detective who deduces details about Gabrielle's husband from clues such as her wedding ring and the return address on her letters.
entities.summary: A brilliant consulting detective with exceptional intellect and eccentric habits returns to 221B Baker Street with Watson, seeking challenging cases while engaging in scientific studies and violin playing, often clashing with Watson over his methods and lifestyle.

entities.name: Dr. Watson
entities.description: Holmes's companion who assists during Gabrielle's consultation by offering her coffee and engaging in discussion about the case.
entities.summary: Holmes's companion, a physician and chronicler, documents their life at Baker Street, reflects on Holmes's experiments and habits, and prepares to leave to resume medical practice.

entities.name: Wedding Ring
entities.description: A copper wedding ring given to Gabrielle by her husband Emile, which Holmes uses to deduce his occupation and origin.
entities.summary: A copper wedding ring given to Gabrielle by her husband Emile, which Holmes uses to deduce his occupation and origin.

entities.name: bundle of letters
entities.description: A collection of correspondence between Gabrielle and her husband that ceases three weeks ago, serving as key evidence in the investigation.

entities.name: Jonah Limited
entities.description: An English company that allegedly employed Emile Valladon after his invention of a new air pump, later discovered to have no verifiable existence.

entities.name: Gabrielle recounts being attacked and rescued from the water
entities.description: Gabrielle describes being ambushed from behind, subdued with chloroform, thrown into the water, and subsequently rescued by an unknown man who wrapped her in a blanket.

entities.name: Holmes deduces an attempt on Gabrielle's life
entities.description: Holmes concludes from Gabrielle's account that she was the target of a deliberate assassination attempt the previous night.

entities.name: Holmes instructs Gabrielle to send a letter to Emile Valladon
entities.description: Holmes directs Gabrielle to write and address a letter to her husband at the Ashdown Street address, guiding her through the process.

entities.name: Holmes prepares and seals a blank letter for delivery
entities.description: Holmes folds a blank sheet of paper, inserts it into the addressed envelope, and begins sealing it to create a test communication.

entities.name: Watson questions the purpose of sending an empty letter
entities.description: Watson expresses skepticism about sending a blank letter to a known non-existent company at an empty storefront, highlighting the apparent futility.

entities.name: Holmes theorizes about the function of the Ashdown Street address
entities.description: Holmes proposes that the empty shop at Ashdown Street serves as a letter-drop or accommodation address where correspondence is collected by an unknown party for an unknown reason.

entities.name: last night
entities.description: A relative temporal expression indicating the time when Gabrielle was attacked, anchoring the event to the night before the current scene.

entities.name: Holmes's office
entities.description: The interior setting where Gabrielle is consulting with Holmes and Watson, implied by the presence of a desk, chair with writing arm, and ongoing consultation.

entities.name: man who rescued Gabrielle
entities.description: An unidentified man who saved Gabrielle from the water after her attack and wrapped her in a blanket.

entities.name: Blank Sheet Of Paper
entities.description: A sheet of paper with no writing on it, prepared by Holmes to be sent as part of a trap to identify who collects mail at the Ashdown Street address.
entities.summary: A sheet of paper with no writing on it, prepared by Holmes to be sent as part of a trap to identify who collects mail at the Ashdown Street address.

entities.name: letter-drop
entities.description: A covert method of communication where letters are left at a designated address for pickup by a third party, used here as a suspected mechanism for receiving messages at the Ashdown Street location.

document_metadata.title: 71、INT. DUNGEON - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Queen Victoria orders HMS Jonah destroyed, dismisses air threats; Mycroft proposes luring Germans to claim the submarine, planning to sink it with them aboard, enlisting Holmes via his connection to Fraulein von Hoffmanstal.

entities.name: Royal party descends spiral staircase into underground submarine chamber
entities.description: The royal party, led by Mycroft, descends a spiral iron staircase into a rock chamber housing a small submarine, marking the beginning of a demonstration for Queen Victoria.

entities.name: Naval officer snaps to attention upon arrival of royal party
entities.description: As the royal party enters the chamber, the commanding naval officer immediately assumes a formal stance of attention in salute.

entities.name: Midget crew raises detachable monster head to reveal conning tower
entities.description: The four surviving midget sailors pull a chain to lift the fake monster's head and neck from the submarine's conning tower, exposing the periscope and true structure of H.M.S. JONAH.

entities.name: Queen Victoria questions purpose of submarine's monster decoy
entities.description: Queen Victoria inquires about the function of the grotesque gargoyle-like head on the submarine, expressing curiosity and mild amusement.

entities.name: Mycroft explains decoy function and introduces submarine demonstration
entities.description: Mycroft informs the Queen that the monster head is a decoy and announces that the crew will now demonstrate the operation of the submersible.

entities.name: Normal-sized sailor commands crew to stand to
entities.description: A full-sized sailor on the submarine's deck issues the command 'Stand to,' initiating the operational demonstration of the vessel.

entities.name: Midget crew enters submarine through hatch
entities.description: Following the command, the midget sailors quickly descend into the submarine via the hatch to assume their operational stations.

entities.name: Queen Victoria comments on sailors' small stature and medal ceremony difficulty
entities.description: The Queen remarks that the sailors are unusually small and jokes that it is tiring to pin medals on them while standing on tiptoe.

entities.name: Submarine engines start, creating noise and activity inside vessel
entities.description: The submarine's engines are activated, resulting in a loud and chaotic environment with machinery operating, acid reactions, and bellows moving.

entities.name: Mycroft guides Queen into submarine and explains key systems
entities.description: Mycroft leads Queen Victoria into the submarine through an open bulkhead and begins describing the main engine, stabilizers, compressor, ballast trimmer, and air-pump.

entities.name: Queen Victoria expresses fondness for canaries aboard submarine
entities.description: The Queen points out the cage of chirping canaries and remarks that they must make the crew feel at home, finding them charming.

entities.name: Mycroft demonstrates torpedo firing levers and periscope functionality
entities.description: Mycroft shows the Queen the controls for launching torpedoes, noting their accuracy up to 120 feet, and points out the periscope used for surface scanning.

entities.name: Royal Demonstration Of H.M.S. Jonah Submarine
entities.description: A formal presentation of the experimental submarine H.M.S. JONAH to Queen Victoria and her entourage, conducted by Mycroft and naval personnel in an underground chamber accessible from Loch Ness.
entities.summary: A formal presentation of the experimental submarine H.M.S. JONAH to Queen Victoria and her entourage, conducted by Mycroft and naval personnel in an underground chamber accessible from Loch Ness.

entities.name: entrance from the Loch

entities.name: H.M.S. Jonah

document_metadata.title: 71、INT. DUNGEON - NIGHT
document_metadata.summary: Queen Victoria orders HMS Jonah destroyed, dismisses air threats; Mycroft proposes luring Germans to claim the submarine, planning to sink it with them aboard, enlisting Holmes via his connection to Fraulein von Hoffmanstal.
